city: Dublin (IADT Dún Laoghaire), Lisbon (Universidade Lusófona), Vilnius (Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre)
institution: FilmEU consortium: Institute of Art, Design + Technology (IADT, coordinator), Universidade Lusófona, Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (LMTA)
program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound / Sound Design for Media Arts
qualification: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts. Described on the official site as a 'Joint Masters Degree in Sound' delivered by the FilmEU consortium — i.e. a single JOINT award, not a double or multiple national degree. UNVERIFIED: the site does not print the exact award-structure wording (single joint parchment vs. co-signed).
accreditationStatus: Selected and funded under Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM), Erasmus+. Listed at IADT as course code DL935. Part of the FilmEU European University alliance.
institutionType: Public higher education institutions / national arts academies (consortium)
durationEcts: 2 years, 4 semesters. QUOTE: 'This two-year, four-semester journey'. 120 ECTS UNVERIFIED — not printed on the pages fetched, though all 24-month EMJM programmes are 120 ECTS by regulation.
whatYouStudy: Sound as an artistic, cultural and technological force across media arts, immersive environments, performance and audiovisual industries. Structured around three conceptual pillars: Societal, Skills, Creative. Sound design, production, composition and research for film, television, gaming, immersive media, technology and virtual environments.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'ReSound is open to both European and non-European students who hold a bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, or media studies.' Also required: motivation letter, and typically two academic or professional references.
acceptsNonMusic: CONDITIONALLY YES. QUOTE: applicants with degrees in other fields 'may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies.' ASSESSMENT FOR THIS CANDIDATE: a BSc Software Engineering is not disqualifying, but admission is explicitly conditioned on demonstrable prior sound/music/film/media experience, which he does not yet have. The portfolio is the gate — this programme is reachable only if he builds a real body of work before applying.
portfolioSpec: QUOTE: 'Applicants should supply no more than 3 examples, with a short reflective paragraph on each piece explicitly stating your role in the work. You can supply a single hyperlink to a portfolio website or a compilation audio or video file. The team can realistically listen/watch 10-15 minutes of material per application, so please select the best work.'
auditionSpec: NO live audition. Online interview for shortlisted candidates only. QUOTE: applicants scoring highest from the application package 'will be called for an online Interview on a date to be settled by the selection committee.'
tuitionNonEU: 15,000 EUR total for self-funded students (no EU/non-EU split published). QUOTE: '7,500 EUR before the beginning of the first semester and 7,500 EUR to be paid before the beginning of the third semester.' EMJM scholarship holders pay NO tuition.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — no application fee found on the official pages. Tunisian nationals must budget separately for three separate visa/residence-permit processes (Ireland, Portugal, Lithuania) — these are meant to be covered from the monthly allowance and are not reimbursed separately.
totalCostEstimate: 0 EUR net if awarded the EMJM scholarship (tuition waived and 1,400 EUR/month received, i.e. net positive up to ~33,600 EUR). Approx. 15,000 EUR tuition plus ~24 months living costs in Dublin/Lisbon/Vilnius if self-funded.
scholarships: 1,400 EUR per month for up to 24 months (up to 33,600 EUR) PLUS full tuition waiver. Maximum 24 places on the programme each year; 'a significant percentage' of successful candidates receive the scholarship — EXACT NUMBER OF SCHOLARSHIPS UNVERIFIED (not published on the official site). Third-party aggregator sites additionally claim 'travel money EUR 2,000 to EUR 3,000 per year, health insurance and installation allowance of EUR 1,000' — UNVERIFIED and inconsistent with current EMJM 2021-2027 rules, under which the 1,400 EUR/month unit contribution is all-inclusive of travel, visa, installation and subsistence. Do not rely on the extra travel figures. TUNISIA: an Erasmus+ Partner Country — a Tunisian competes in the non-EU/Partner Country pool, and EMJM rules cap how many scholarships may go to nationals of any one country.
languageRequirement: English only. No Portuguese, Irish or Lithuanian required. Candidate's Arabic and French are irrelevant to eligibility here.
englishTest: QUOTE: 'IELTS 6.0 or Equivalent (no component less than 6.0)', or equivalent TOEFL iBT / Duolingo / Cambridge / LanguageCert score, taken 'within the last two years.' Alternative route: evidence of 'a full qualification min Level 4 European Qualifications Framework (EQF) and minimum duration one academic year through the instruction of English.'
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026 intake): opened 20 October 2025, deadline 27 January 2026 — CLOSED. Official site now states: 'Applications for ReSound 2026 have now closed.' EXPECTED 2027-CYCLE WINDOW: opens approx. mid-to-late October 2026; closes approx. late January 2027. NOT YET PUBLISHED — re-check the site from October 2026. NO DEADLINE BEFORE SEPTEMBER 2026.
applicationOpens: Expected approx. October 2026 for the September 2027 intake (prior cycle opened 20 October 2025). UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle.
requiresAdmissionFirst: NO. Money is decided INSIDE the single admission process — one application covers both admission and the EMJM scholarship. The selection committee ranks applicants and awards scholarships from the admitted pool. No separate scholarship form, no separate earlier scholarship deadline. The scholarship is NOT automatic on admission: it is competitive within the admitted cohort.

institution: Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne (coordinator), Universidade Católica Portuguesa — School of Arts Porto, University of Silesia in Katowice
program: DIGICREA — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master 'Digital Creativity, Art & Science' — SOUND-MUSIC specialization path
qualification: MULTIPLE NATIONAL DEGREES (not a single joint award). QUOTE: graduates receive a Master degree from all three institutions — 'Master of Arts in Contemporary Creation and New Technologies' (Université Jean Monnet), 'Master in Sound and Image' (UCP Porto), 'Music in Multimedia' (University of Silesia).
accreditationStatus: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM), Erasmus+ funded. First cohort 2025-2026; currently running its 2026-2028 cohort.
institutionType: Two public universities + one Catholic (private, state-recognised) university
durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS. Semester 1 Saint-Étienne, Semester 2 Porto, Semester 3 Katowice, Semester 4 internship/thesis with public and private sector partners.
whatYouStudy: Digital creativity at the intersection of art, technology and science: audio-visual new media, digital technologies, film, MUSIC, graphics, artificial intelligence, virtual and extended reality. Applicants choose ONE specialization path: SOUND-MUSIC or Image. Concludes with an industry internship.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS is the minimum requirement to enrol.' Candidates holding 150 ECTS at application may be considered if they provide 'a sworn statement that 180 ECTS will be obtained before the start of the programme.' QUOTE: applicants must 'apply for one specialization path only'. Required documents include a 'Science qualification form describing mathematics, programming, and technical skills', Europass CV in English, certified bachelor diploma with English translation, university transcripts with ECTS, a 2-minute video presentation, minimum two letters of recommendation in English, and an English certificate.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — STRONGEST STRUCTURAL FIT FOUND IN THIS SWEEP. The programme places no restriction on the bachelor's field of study; the only degree requirement quoted is 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS is the minimum requirement to enrol.' Crucially, one of the mandatory documents is a 'Science qualification form describing mathematics, programming, and technical skills' — a BSc Software Engineering is a POSITIVE ASSET here rather than a handicap, which is the opposite of the conservatoire route. The portfolio remains mandatory and is still the real gate.
portfolioSpec: QUOTE: 'exactly 3 to 5 specific works or project (video/audio/images) including metadata (title, short description, public link, and their role).' All projects must be 'not more than 5 years old.' For the Sound-Music path: composition, sound design, or music pieces. Separately required: a video presentation of 'max 2 minutes'.
auditionSpec: NO live audition and no instrumental performance test. QUOTE: selected applicants proceed to 'Stage II' with 'an online 15-minute interview.'
tuitionNonEU: ZERO. QUOTE: 'Students (scholarship holders and non-scholarship holders) are not charged any tuition fees.' Applies identically to EU and non-EU students — unusual among EMJMs and highly favourable for a self-funded fallback.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — no application fee found. Self-funded students 'must provide proof of financial support' for living costs across three countries. Three separate visa/residence processes (France, Portugal, Poland) at the candidate's own cost.
totalCostEstimate: 0 EUR tuition in all cases. With EMJM scholarship: net positive, up to 33,600 EUR received. Without scholarship: living costs only (Saint-Étienne, Porto, Katowice are all comparatively low-cost cities).
scholarshipName: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) Scholarship — DIGICREA
scholarships: QUOTE: 'a grant of 1,400 euros per month, for a total duration of 24 months' = maximum 33,600 EUR per recipient. QUOTE: the monthly stipend addresses 'Travel costs; Visa costs; Installation costs; Subsistence costs' — confirming the all-inclusive EMJM unit-cost model with no separate travel top-up. QUOTE: 'a limited number of EMJM scholarships per cohort' — EXACT NUMBER UNVERIFIED. Third-party reporting claims roughly 75% of students are funded — UNVERIFIED against the official site, treat with caution. QUOTE: 'Candidates who have previously received an EMJM scholarship are not eligible for EMJM Digicrea scholarship.' TUNISIA: Partner Country — competes in the non-EU pool under EMJM per-country caps.
languageRequirement: English. QUOTE: 'A certified level test in English at least B2, note that C1 recommended.' No French or Portuguese requirement despite the French coordinator — but the candidate's fluent French is a practical advantage for daily life in Saint-Étienne and for the internship semester.
englishTest: QUOTE: accepted tests are 'IELTS 6, TOEFL ITP 550, TOEFL IBT (at least 90), TOEIC (at least 650).' Minimum B2, C1 recommended. Exemption if the prior degree was 'taught and conducted 100% in English' or the applicant is a native English speaker. WARNING: the stated TOEFL iBT bar of 90 is high for a 'working English' candidate — but IELTS 6 is a far softer equivalent route and is the one to target.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2026-2028 cohort): opened 14 November 2025, closed 16 February 2026 — CLOSED. FOR THE 2027 INTAKE, QUOTE FROM THE OFFICIAL SITE: 'The call for applications for the next DIGICREA cohort 2027-2029 is expected to open in November 2026.' Closing therefore expected approx. mid-February 2027 by analogy with the prior cycle. NO DEADLINE BEFORE SEPTEMBER 2026.
applicationOpens: November 2026 (expected — stated on the official site) for the 2027-2029 cohort.
requiresAdmissionFirst: NO. One combined application. QUOTE: the scholarship application is integrated into the main programme application and 'no separate submission is required.' The award is NOT automatic on admission — it depends on the selection committee's ranking among eligible admitted applicants. No separate earlier scholarship deadline.

institution: Royal Conservatoire of Antwerp (RCA), Escola Superior de Música e Artes do Espetáculo (ESMAE) Porto, Lietuvos Muzikos ir Teatro Akademija (LMTA) Vilnius
program: RESONO — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in collaborative music creation and performance
qualification: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master degree, awarded across the three conservatoires. UNVERIFIED whether a single joint parchment or multiple national degrees — the site says 'joint master' but does not print the award structure.
accreditationStatus: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM). QUOTE from the official site: 'Co-funded by the European Union'.
durationEcts: QUOTE: 'Two academic years, culminating in 120 ECTS credits.' One semester at each of Antwerp, Porto and Vilnius.
whatYouStudy: Collaborative music creation and performance. HIGHLY RELEVANT MODULE LIST — the curriculum explicitly includes 'Spatial Audio for Music Composition and Studio Production', 'Electronic Composition', 'Sound Art', 'Composition for Stage' and 'Screen scoring', alongside RESONO Lab, RESONO Project and Artistic Research. This is the only conservatoire-consortium EMJM found with a named electronic-composition and sound-art content.
entryRequirements: UNVERIFIED — the official admission page does not publish a degree requirement, and no statement about accepting non-music bachelors was found. Given that all three partners are conservatoires and the portfolio demands demonstrated instrumental/vocal/compositional level, a prior music qualification or equivalent demonstrable conservatoire-level practice should be assumed necessary.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — and PROBABLY NOT in practice. No wording accepting non-music bachelors was found on the official pages (unlike ReSound, DIGICREA and DocNomadsPlus, all of which print such a clause). The required portfolio explicitly asks for 'the level of instrumental or vocal skills' and 'the level of composition/creation', which a candidate with no conservatoire training and no portfolio cannot currently evidence. TREAT AS EFFECTIVELY CLOSED to this candidate unless he first builds a substantial composition portfolio, and confirm directly with the consortium.
portfolioSpec: QUOTE: 'A portfolio that reflects the level of instrumental or vocal skills, including electronics, supported by relevant documents and video material' AND 'A portfolio that reflects the level of composition/creation and creative identity of the candidate, supported by relevant documents and audio or video material.' Note the phrase 'including electronics' — electronic practice is explicitly admissible as the instrument.
auditionSpec: YES — AUDITION REQUIRED, but ONLINE not in person. QUOTE: 'Step 2: Interview and audition' — 'Candidates who make it through the first round will meet online with jury members from the three institutions.' The audition also serves as the English check: QUOTE: 'An interview that will test the level of English.' Candidates also prepare a project concept for the entrance exam.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — not published on the pages fetched.
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED. EMJM scholarship holders would pay no tuition and receive the standard allowance.
scholarships: Erasmus Mundus scholarships available, covering tuition and living expenses. EXACT AMOUNT, MONTHLY STIPEND AND NUMBER OF PLACES UNVERIFIED — not published on the official pages fetched. The EMJM standard is 1,400 EUR/month plus tuition waiver, but this was NOT confirmed on the RESONO site. Tunisia is a Partner Country and would compete in the non-EU pool.
languageRequirement: English. No published test score — proficiency is assessed live in the audition interview.
englishTest: UNVERIFIED — no numeric test score published. QUOTE: the audition includes 'An interview that will test the level of English.' This is unusual and favourable: it may mean no formal IELTS/TOEFL certificate is required.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no deadline published on the official pages fetched. EMJM scholarship deadlines in this family typically fall between early December and end of January. EXPECTED 2027-CYCLE WINDOW: approx. November 2026 to January/February 2027. MUST BE CONFIRMED DIRECTLY WITH THE CONSORTIUM.
requiresAdmissionFirst: UNVERIFIED — the two-step structure (application screening, then interview and audition) implies a single combined process typical of EMJM, but this was not confirmed on the official site.

institution: Universidade Lusófona (coordinator), Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre — National Film School KIMO, LUCA School of Arts Brussels
program: DocNomadsPlus — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree in Documentary Film Directing
qualification: Joint Master's degree, 120 credits. Successor programme to DocNomads (2012-2025). UNVERIFIED whether a single joint parchment or multiple national degrees.
accreditationStatus: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM), Erasmus+ funded; renewed as 'DocNomadsPlus' for the cycle covering the September 2027 intake.
durationEcts: 2 years, full-time, 120 credits. Semesters sequentially in Lisbon, Vilnius and Brussels; 4th semester back in one of the three.
whatYouStudy: Advanced training for international independent documentary film directors. RELEVANCE CAVEAT: this is film DIRECTING, not electronic music. Included in this sweep because it is a fully funded joint programme in the same FilmEU/creative-arts family and because its 2027 deadline structure is the clearest funding-timeline trap found. It is a POOR subject fit for an aspiring electronic music producer.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree required. Preferred backgrounds: 'Film Studies, Audiovisual Arts, Media / Communication studies.' QUOTE: 'Applicants with a Bachelor's degree in other fields may also be considered, provided they submit a convincing artistic portfolio.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES for non-film and non-arts degrees. QUOTE: 'Applicants with a Bachelor's degree in other fields may also be considered, provided they submit a convincing artistic portfolio.' But the portfolio demanded is documentary film work, not music — so the openness does not help this candidate's actual goal.
portfolioSpec: Three video submissions: a 1-minute motivation video; a 3-minute documentary on the set theme 'Around Me, in the Here and Now'; and a link to one previous film (max 10 minutes).
auditionSpec: NO live audition. Online interview, QUOTE: 'approximately 15-20 minutes' per candidate, scheduled over three days.
tuitionNonEU: 15,000 EUR for the complete four-semester programme, paid in three installments. Scholarship holders pay no tuition fees.
totalCostEstimate: 0 EUR net with EMJM scholarship; approx. 15,000 EUR plus living costs if self-funded.
scholarships: 1,400 EUR per month plus full tuition waiver. NUMBER OF SCHOLARSHIPS UNVERIFIED — the official page does not state it. Tunisians eligible in the Partner Country pool under EMJM per-country caps.
englishTest: QUOTE: 'The minimum required level of the English proficiency certificates is B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR).' Accepted: IELTS 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 79+, Cambridge 170+, Duolingo 110+, ITACE.
deadline: CONFIRMED FOR THE SEPTEMBER 2027 INTAKE ON THE OFFICIAL SITE — TWO SEPARATE DEADLINES. QUOTE: 'January 2027 – for candidates applying for Erasmus Mundus scholarships' and 'April 2027 – for self-funded applicants only'. EXACT DAY IN JANUARY 2027 NOT YET PUBLISHED. THIS IS THE CRITICAL TIMELINE TRAP: an applicant who waits for the visible April deadline forfeits all scholarship consideration and can only enter self-funded. NO DEADLINE BEFORE SEPTEMBER 2026.
requiresAdmissionFirst: NO separate scholarship application form, BUT the funded track has its own EARLIER DEADLINE (January 2027) distinct from the ordinary self-funded deadline (April 2027). Funding is therefore effectively gated by an earlier application date, not by prior admission.

durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS (UNVERIFIED on the page fetched). Students spend semesters at three different universities plus one associated partner.

acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY. QUOTE: 'Other fields will be taken into consideration by the Application Board' — the programme does not require the first degree to be in a specific field. Of all programmes in this sweep this has the most open degree-subject rule.
portfolioSpec: NO conventional creative portfolio required — a major advantage for a candidate with no portfolio. Instead: QUOTE: 'Example of relevant work. (academic paper, cultural project, art work) (max 5 pages)' plus an essay on media arts culture trends. A written academic paper from his BSc could satisfy this.
auditionSpec: NO audition. No interview requirement is mentioned in the application materials.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — not specified for non-EU students on the page fetched.
scholarships: Erasmus+/Erasmus Mundus scholarships stated as possibly available for the 2026-2028 intake; the site notes they are 'available to all prospective students, regardless of nationality' and 'HIGHLY COMPETITIVE'. englishTest: QUOTE: 'TOEFL iBT: 80 | Cambridge C1 | IELTS (academic): 6.5 | Versant: 56-60.' Results must be 'less than 2 years old.' Waived if the prior degree was taught in English.
deadline: PRIOR/CURRENT CYCLE: QUOTE from the official site: 'Rules and dates for application will be available in February 2026' for the 2026-2028 intake — i.e. this programme publishes late and runs a spring application window, unlike the October-January EMJM norm. EXPECTED 2027-CYCLE WINDOW: rules published approx. early 2027, application window approx. spring 2027 — BUT NOTE the programme recruits on a two-year cycle (2026-2028 intake), so THERE MAY BE NO SEPTEMBER 2027 INTAKE AT ALL. UNVERIFIED AND CRITICAL — must be confirmed directly.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle. Possible that the next intake after 2026-2028 is 2028-2030.
requiresAdmissionFirst: UNVERIFIED — presumed single combined application per EMJM norm, but not confirmed on the page fetched.

country: Germany + Netherlands (bilateral double degree, NOT Erasmus Mundus)
institution: Technische Universität Berlin — Audio Communication Group (year 1) and Royal Conservatoire The Hague / University of the Arts — Institute of Sonology (year 2)
program: Audio Communication and Sonology — Master's double degree specialisation
qualification: TRUE DOUBLE DEGREE. QUOTE: graduates obtain 'a Master of Science from the TU Berlin and a Master of Music in Sonology from the Royal Conservatoire.' Two separate national degrees, one from each institution.
accreditationStatus: Nationally accredited German M.Sc. and Dutch Master of Music, joined by a bilateral exchange agreement. NOT an Erasmus Mundus programme and carries NO bundled scholarship.
institutionType: Public technical university + public university of the arts / conservatoire
language: GERMAN is the main language of year 1. QUOTE from TU Berlin: 'The main language of instruction in the Master's programme is German.' Year 2 (Sonology, The Hague) is in English.
durationEcts: 2 years. Year 1 in Berlin on the Audio Communication and Technology M.Sc. (60 ECTS), year 2 at Sonology in The Hague. Total ECTS UNVERIFIED.
whatYouStudy: QUOTE: 'combines a course in the theory of acoustics, audio technology, signal processing and musicology at the Audio Communication department of the TU Berlin with in-depth study of the artistic aspects of electroacoustic music and sound art at Sonology in The Hague.' Sonology is one of the world's leading electronic/electroacoustic music institutes — subject fit for this candidate is excellent.
entryRequirements: TU Berlin M.Sc. Audio Communication and Technology entry: QUOTE: 'a first university degree in a science, engineering, humanities, social science, arts, business or law programme', plus 'knowledge of higher mathematics (analysis, linear algebra) at the level of the basic lectures of a science or engineering degree (at least 10 LP)' and 'knowledge of a programming language or a computer algebra system'. For the double-degree exchange to The Hague: QUOTE: 'Proficiency in German at least on level TDN 4 / TestDaF of CEFR', 'Mathematical knowledge on engineering basic studies level (Analysis I, Linear Algebra)', 'Knowledge of a programming language or a computer algebra system', plus a research project proposal.
acceptsNonMusic: YES, AND EXCEPTIONALLY WELL SUITED ON PAPER. QUOTE: entry requires 'a first university degree in a science, engineering, humanities, social science, arts, business or law programme' — no music degree is required at all, and the mathematics and programming prerequisites make a BSc Software Engineering close to an ideal profile. NO PORTFOLIO IS REQUIRED for TU Berlin entry, which is unique among the strong-fit options in this sweep. HOWEVER SEE THE LANGUAGE BLOCKER BELOW.
portfolioSpec: NONE FOUND for the TU Berlin entry point. QUOTE: no aptitude test or portfolio requirement is mentioned in the TU Berlin programme description. For the second-year transfer a 'research project proposal' is required. This is the only strong-fit programme in this sweep that appears to require no creative portfolio at entry — UNVERIFIED for the Sonology stage.
auditionSpec: NO live audition found at the TU Berlin entry point. UNVERIFIED for the Sonology second-year admission (Sonology's standalone master normally requires portfolio and interview).
tuitionNonEU: TU Berlin charges NO tuition fees (German public university); QUOTE: students 'must pay a fee per semester to cover the social contribution and the costs of public transport'. EXACT SEMESTER CONTRIBUTION AMOUNT UNVERIFIED (typically a few hundred EUR per semester). Royal Conservatoire The Hague non-EEA tuition for year 2 UNVERIFIED and potentially substantial.
otherFees: German student visa requires proof of funds in a blocked account (Sperrkonto) — amount UNVERIFIED at 2027 rates. Semester contribution at TU Berlin. Dutch residence permit costs for year 2.
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED. Low tuition in Berlin but no stipend attached; the candidate would need separate funding (e.g. DAAD) plus living costs in Berlin and The Hague.
scholarshipName: NONE BUNDLED. No scholarship attaches to this double degree.
scholarships: NO funding is bundled with admission. This is the key weakness: subject fit and entry-requirement fit are both excellent, but the candidate would have to win separate funding. The obvious DAAD route is BLOCKED — see the DAAD record in this file.
languageRequirement: HARD BLOCKER FOR THIS CANDIDATE. QUOTE (TU Berlin programme page): 'The main language of instruction in the Master's programme is German' and 'you will therefore have to prove German skills at level C1'. QUOTE (double-degree page): 'Proficiency in German at least on level TDN 4 / TestDaF'. The candidate has Arabic, French and working English and NO German. Reaching C1/TestDaF-4 German is realistically an 18-24 month full-time undertaking and would have to start immediately to be ready for a September 2027 entry.
englishTest: QUOTE: applicants must 'show proficiency in English at least on a level equivalent to the evaluation scales IELTS (6,0) or TOEFL (ibT level 83)'. English is required IN ADDITION to German C1, not instead of it.
deadline: TU Berlin international application deadline for the M.Sc. UNVERIFIED — German winter-semester master deadlines for international applicants typically fall between 15 January and 15 July, so a deadline BEFORE SEPTEMBER 2026 IS PLAUSIBLE but was not confirmed. For the second-year exchange to The Hague: QUOTE: 'The deadline for application to the exchange is 15 February for the current year' — this applies during year 1 in Berlin, not at initial entry.
requiresAdmissionFirst: YES, IN A TWO-STAGE SENSE. QUOTE: 'Candidates apply in Berlin first. When accepted, they apply for the Sonology master's programme before the beginning of the second semester in Berlin.' The double degree is not applied for directly — the candidate must first be admitted to and enrolled on TU Berlin's Audio Communication and Technology M.Sc., then compete for one of the six exchange places by the 15 February internal deadline. QUOTE: 'There are only six places available on the course' / the Royal Conservatoire 'agrees to accept as a host university each year up to 6 students.'

country: EU-wide (structural finding, not a single programme)
institution: European Commission / EACEA — Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters catalogue
program: STRUCTURAL FINDING: the 37 newly selected EMJM projects starting September 2027
whatYouStudy: The European Commission announced that 37 Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters projects were selected under the latest Erasmus+ call. QUOTE from the official Erasmus+ page: these programmes 'will be opening for student applications in the autumn of 2026 to start programmes in September 2027.' THIS IS EXACTLY THE CANDIDATE'S INTAKE. The official page names only a sample of the 37 and does NOT publish the full list; among the named examples only 'European Master in Animation' is creative-sector. A third-party list (erasmuscatalogue.com, NOT OFFICIAL) enumerates all 37 and contains NO dedicated music, sound design or audio programme in the new cohort — the closest are ReAnima (animation) and WAVES Plus (acoustics and vibration ENGINEERING, a technical not artistic programme). CONCLUSION: the September 2027 opportunity in sound/music rests on the EXISTING catalogue programmes (ReSound, DIGICREA, RESONO), not on the new cohort. The third-party enumeration is UNVERIFIED and the official EACEA catalogue should be re-checked once the 37 are added to it during autumn 2026.
scholarships: GENERAL EMJM RULES RELEVANT TO A TUNISIAN APPLICANT: Tunisia is an Erasmus+ PARTNER COUNTRY (not a Programme Country), so a Tunisian applicant competes in the non-EU pool. Under the EMJM 2021-2027 rules the scholarship is a single all-inclusive unit contribution of 1,400 EUR per month for up to 24 months, PLUS a full waiver of the programme's participation costs. The older EMJMD (2014-2020) model of a separate travel allowance (1,000-3,000 EUR/year) and a 1,000 EUR installation allowance NO LONGER APPLIES to newly funded programmes, although several third-party scholarship websites still quote those figures — these are misleading. EMJM rules also cap the number of scholarships that may be awarded to students of any single nationality, which is why the Partner Country pool is the relevant competition. A candidate may apply to a MAXIMUM OF THREE different EMJM programmes per intake and can hold only one scholarship — UNVERIFIED against the current official rules for the 2027 call and MUST be confirmed before submitting.
deadline: Applications for the 37 new programmes open in AUTUMN 2026 for a September 2027 start. Individual deadlines are set per consortium and are not centrally published. NO CENTRAL EMJM DEADLINE EXISTS — each consortium runs its own.
requiresAdmissionFirst: NO for EMJM generally — the EMJM scholarship is decided within each consortium's single admission process. There is no separate central scholarship application. The consequence for planning: the candidate must apply to each consortium individually, on each consortium's own timetable, and in most cases the scholarship-eligible deadline is the EARLIER of the two deadlines a consortium publishes.
